title: Audit Console: journey replay + contextual download bundles
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Add an 'Audit Journey' feature in the Console that lets admins and authorized auditors: run precise search queries, step through a time-ordered sequence of related audit events (replay), and produce contextual download bundles (CSV/JSON/NDJSON) that include event rows plus linked metadata snapshots (user role at time, affected resources, request headers redacted per policy). Work ties into RBAC v2 to ensure only allowed roles can replay or download sensitive bundles. Deliver both an interactive UI for on-screen investigation and an async export job API for large result sets.
tasks: Design wireframes for journey timeline and row-level context panel (DES-1167)
API: search endpoint with correlated-session grouping and cursor pagination (ENG-20121)
Backend: async export job pipeline supporting CSV/NDJSON bundles with role-aware redaction
Access control: integrate RBAC v2 checks for replay/download actions
Export: signed temporary URL generation and S3-compatible storage retention policy
E2E tests for pagination, sampling, and redaction rules
Telemetry: emit metrics for export job duration, bytes, and denied attempts
Docs: Console guide + API reference + compliance FAQ

acceptance_criteria: Admins with 'audit.viewer' or higher can open 'Audit Journey' for a session and step through events chronologically
Saved queries created by a user are visible to that user's org according to RBAC v2 sharing rules
Export jobs accept a saved query or ad-hoc filters and produce a bundle containing event rows plus contextual metadata JSON per row
Export bundles redact fields according to active redaction policy (PII, auth tokens) before being persisted
Exports for >100k rows run asynchronously; user receives signed download URL with configurable TTL
All replay/download operations are logged as admin-audit events and surface in the Activity dashboard
Frontend handles cursor pagination and shows a stable 'jump-to' index for long sessions without loading entire result set
